calls.title: Nhat vs Johnny (filters)
calls.summary: The team discussed improving the current filter design, which is viewed as confusing and suboptimal. Participants noted that filters behave more like search strings, complicating usability. Nhat suggested separating text search from filters, while Johnny proposed multi-select tags to simplify user interaction. There was debate over filter placement, leaning toward a sidebar to unify the dashboard. Concerns about unclear filter names and inconsistent logic across metrics were raised, with a preference for disabling non-applicable filters to maintain clarity. The goal is to unify dashboards and allow user customization, but any design changes require stakeholder approval to avoid disrupting current workflows. The team emphasized the need for better naming and documentation while planning to gather feedback and iterate design before a September deadline.
calls.keywords: filters, dashboard, experiment metrics, user experience, design system, multi-select

calls.title: Filters
calls.summary: The team addressed the need to simplify and standardize filter UI elements to enhance user experience and maintain product consistency. Key decisions included removing the expansion feature, reverting to known filter buttons to prevent user confusion, and reducing the filter size from height 32 to 24 for a cleaner interface. While filters vary by context, a unified style framework is essential. New filter types were proposed, including dimension filters and ad hoc filters, with discussions on managing visibility based on dashboard blocks. The team also explored various UI patterns to balance usability and scalability, emphasizing the need for clarity in filter labeling and terminology. Follow-ups were planned to refine requirements and ensure the design aligns with the product's design system.
calls.keywords: Filters, Experiments, Dimension Filters, Ad Hoc Filters, UI Consistency, Dashboard
